 Judgment
Heard the learned Additional SPP appearing for the appellant - State and the learned counsel appearing for the respondent - accused.

2. The factual matrix of the case of the prosecution before the trial Court is as under:
2.1

That on 24.07.2018 at around 6.30 p.m. the respondent - accused took the victim girl near the haystack in the backyard of the house of Gobbaradavar and committed forcible penetrative sexual assault upon the victim girl knowing fully well that she was a minor (below the age 12 years) and hence penal offences of Section 376 of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act have been invoked.

2.2 The prosecution, in order to prove its case against the accused since he did not plead guilty and NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB claimed trial, examined PW.1 to PW.17 and also got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and MO.1 to MO.14.

2.3 The trial Court having considered both oral and documentary evidence available on record, comes to the conclusion that the prosecution is unable to prove the case against the accused for the offence invoked against him and benefit of doubt was given in favour of the accused and acquitted the accused of the offences invoked against him.
3. Being aggrieved by the judgment of acquittal, the present appeal is filed by the State contending that the trial Court has failed to consider the evidence of PW.1 and State Of Karnataka vs Anand S/O Fakkirappa Bammigatti on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138616978/
2 PW.2 who are the parents of the victim girl, PW.4 who is the victim girl who is aged three years eight months, PW.3 and PW.8 who are the grandmothers of the victim girl, PW.15 who is the uncle of victim girl and PW.10 who is the doctor who has examined the victim girl and issued medical certificate.

The learned Additional SPP contends that all these witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution, but the trial Court without proper appreciation of evidence of these witnesses, has committed an error in acquitting the accused.

5. The learned Additional SPP also in his argument vehemently contend that when PW.4 - victim girl supported the case of the prosecution and clearly stated about the commission of sexual assault by the accused, the trial Court ought to have appreciated the evidence on record particularly the evidence of PW.1, PW.2, PW.3 and PW.8 which corroborates the evidence of PW.4.

He also submits that the medical evidence also supports the case of the prosecution, where the doctor has found bite marks on the left cheek of the victim girl and issued the wound certificate in terms of Ex.P.12.
The same is also not considered by the trial Court.
Hence, he would vehemently contend that this Court has to reverse the finding of the trial Court and convict the respondent - accused.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent - accused would vehemently contend that the trial Court in detail has considered the material on record and passed the well reasoned judgment in appreciation of the evidence of the witnesses.

The trial Court found material contradictions in the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 as well as in the evidence of PW.3 and PW.8 i.e. the evidence of grandmothers and also taken note of the opinion of the doctor who categorically opined that no injuries were found on the private part of the victim girl and though an allegation is made that there were injuries on the private part of the victim girl, the same is not found.
7.
Counsel also vehemently contend that the victim - PW.4 who has been examined before the Court has also not identified the accused.

He also contends that though doctor - PW.10 opined that there is a bite mark on the cheek of the victim girl, the same is also taken note of by the trial Court and the trial Court has considered the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB CD which clearly disclosed recording of statement of victim and no such injury was found in the said CD evidencing the fact of bite mark.

He submits that all these materials are considered by the trial Court and hence no reasons are made out to set aside the judgment of acquittal and to convict the accused of the offences which have been invoked against him.

8. Having heard the learned Additional SPP and also the counsel appearing for respondent and having considered the oral evidence of PW.1 to PW.17 and documentary evidence, material objects and also the grounds urged in the appeal, the following point would arise for consideration:

3 i. Whether the trial Court has committed an error in acquitting the accused instead of convicting the accused of the offences which have been invoked against him?

9. Having heard the respective counsel, the material on record discloses that the prosecution mainly relies upon the oral evidence of PW.1 to PW.17 and NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB documentary evidence of Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.

It is also the case of the prosecution that the accused took the victim girl to the vacant place of backyard of Gobbaradavar and committed forcible penetrative sexual assault on her and as a result Sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act have been invoked.
10. Having perused the evidence available on record, PW.1 is the mother of the victim girl.

She has narrated that on 24.07.2018 herself and her children went to the house of CW.11 and CW.11 i.e.
mother-in-law asked her to prepare food and when she was preparing the food, she came out from the kitchen and did not find the victim and on enquiry, she came to know that the victim girl had went to the house of neighbors to play with children.
Thereafter, the victim girl came to house with sludge hands and legs.
She states that CW.11 cleaned the hands and legs of the victim girl.

The victim girl asked for attending the nature call, but she passed latrine in her nicker itself and while cleaning the latrine, they found NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB bleeding injury over anus of the victim girl but they thought that she fell down somewhere and has sustained injury and she was treated in their house itself.
11. PW.1 further states that on the next day i.e. on 25.07.2018 in the morning, she found swelling over the cheek of the victim girl and she had asked victim girl about the injury.

At that time the victim girl told that Anandanna bite her and also caused injury over her anus and then the victim girl took them to the backyard of Gobbaradavar and showed the spot where the accused committed sexual intercourse upon her and thereafter she was taken to the hospital and treatment was provided to her and thereafter, she lodged the complaint on 01.08.2018.
12.
The other witness is PW.2 who is the husband of PW.1 and father of the victim girl.
He also reiterates the same in his chief evidence.
The victim girl is PW.4 and before the Court she says that while playing Anandanna took her to somewhere and committed "".
She had informed the said fact to her mother.
When it was asked her as to where she has been subjected to the said act, she showed both her cheeks, anus and private part and says Anandanna committed "" upon those places.
14. The prosecution also relied upon the evidence of PW.8 who is the grandmother of the victim girl.
She also reiterates the same.

15. PW.15 is the uncle of the victim girl and he is a hearsay witness and he states that he came to know about the said incident when CW.1 was talking that CW.8 has sustained injury and they took her to hospital and lodged the complaint.
PW.3 is the also grandmother of the victim girl and she reiterated that the victim girl was weeping.

The trial Court has taken note of all main witnesses of the prosecution i.e. PW.1, PW.2, PW.3,
PW.8 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB and PW.15 and all of them are relative witnesses and it is important to note that according to the complainant the incident has taken place on 24.07.2018 and at that time they have not noticed any bite injury on the face of the girl but only on the next day i.e. on 25.07.2018 they found swelling on the cheek and on enquiry the victim girl - PW.4 revealed the same but PW.4 has not revealed the same on 24.07.2018 and the evidence of witnesses is also clear that according to them she was subjected to sexual act.
17. The prosecution also examined the doctor who had examined the victim girl.
He deposed before the Court that she had not found any such injury over the anus or private part of the victim girl but only found bite injury.
PW.8 evidence is not in respect of any injury found in her anus.
The other witness is PW.9 who has also examined the accused and he also says that he has not found any sign of sexual injury.
18. Having considered the evidence, particularly PW.10 - doctor, it is very clear that no injuries are found - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB over the anus or private part of the victim girl.
But PW.1, PW.2 and PW.8 speaks that there were injuries on the anus of the victim girl.
The said evidence is contrary to the medial evidence.

The trial Court has also taken note of the medical evidence and the same is contrary to the evidence of PW.1, PW.2 and PW.8 and PW.1, PW.2 and PW.8 and PW.15 have deposed contrary to each other and they have not disclosed about the treatment provided to the victim girl after the alleged incident before the Investigating Officer and the Investigating Officer has not recorded statement of any such doctor.

19. Further, it is important to note that PW.1 deposed that she took victim girl before a male doctor,
PW.2 deposed that the victim girl was taken before a lady doctor, PW.8 deposed that they took the victim girl before a doctor and PW.15 deposed before the Court that victim girl was taken to Noolvi doctor and the same has been discussed in paragraph No.26 of the impugned judgment.

The material on record does not disclose that the victim - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB was taken to the hospital for treatment on the next date of the alleged incident itself and all of them say that they have treated the victim in the house itself on the date of incident.
The witnesses have also not disclosed these facts before the Investigating Officer that victim girl was taken to the hospital but the complaint was given on 01.08.2018.

sentences.text: It is also important to note that, even if they found the injury on 25.07.2018 and the victim girl disclosed the same on 25.07.2018, nothing prevented them to lodge a complaint immediately upon coming to know about the said incident.
Apart from that, the victim was taken to the hospital on 01.08.2018.
The medical evidence also does not support the case of the prosecution that the victim was subjected to sexual act by the accused.
The evidence of PW.9 also does not suggest anything about the accused subjecting the victim girl for sexual act.

No injuries are found and the victim girl is aged about only three years eight months and if she was - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB subjected to sexual act by the accused, there would have injury to the accused also and the same is also not found.
21. The evidence of PW.9 and PW.10, doctors who had examined the victim as well as accused, not stated anything about subjecting her for sexual act.
The evidence of PW.1, PW.2, PW.8 and PW.15 is also contradictory to each other.

The Trial Court has also taken note of evidence of PW.1 and during the cross-examination she deposed that prior to lodging of first information with the police, she took the victim girl to private hospital which is nearby their house and the doctor injected the victim girl and he is a male doctor.

22. PW.2 deposed in his chief evidence that he himself, his mother and his wife took the victim girl for treatment near the house, but the doctor adviced to take victim girl to other hospital and this fact also taken note by the Trial Court while appreciating the evidence.
But during the cross examination deposed that they took the victim girl to lady doctor and not given any injection and - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB tablets and so also not examined her.

But this fact has not been stated before the police during the course of investigation and Investigating Officer also not recorded the statement of doctor who treated the victim immediately when the victim girl was taken to the hospital.
23. These are the material facts taken note by the Trial Court in detail.
Taking note of the fact that even the victim also not identified the accused and well reasons are given while acquitting the accused by the trial Court.
Taking note of the contents of the document at Ex.P.1 wherein, the allegation is made against this accused/respondent.

In paragraph Nos.22 to 27 of the judgment discloses the appreciation of evidence of witnesses in detail and hence the Trial Court rightly comes to the conclusion that the prosecution has not made out the case to invoke the offences which have been invoked against the accused/respondent.

Even the Trial Court also taken note of Sections 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act to - 15 - State Of Karnataka vs Anand S/O Fakkirappa Bammigatti on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138616978/
6 NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB invoke the presumption under the Act about the commission of offences by the accused and culpable mind of the accused and hold that the Court can draw such presumption.
24. Having taken note of both oral and documentary evidence available on record and also medical evidence which not supported the case of the prosecution.

sentences.text: There are many inconsistencies of evidence in the case of the prosecution witnesses.

When such material available before the Court and also when the Trial Court also taken note of material available on record and finding given that inconsistency in the material evidence on record and the evidence placed before the Trial Court not inspires the confidence of the Court.

Having considered the grounds urged in the appeal and also considering relevant submissions of learned Additional State Public Prosecutor and also the respondent there is no any consistent evidence which corroborate the offence on victim girl and the evidence of victim girl, her father, her - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:13181-DB mother and grand-mother also inconsistent, apart from medical evidence.
25. In the absence of consistent evidence and inspiring evidence before the Court, the question of coming to other conclusion does not arise.
Hence, we do not find any merit in this appeal to set aside the judgment of acquittal passed against the accused/respondent.
Hence, we answer the point as negative.

26. In view of the observation made above we pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
Bail bonds executed by the accused and sureties stand cancelled.
